trips.title: Nordkette Skyline, A Running Week Above Innsbruck
trips.summary: Seven days of lift-assisted vertical above Innsbruck, from the Nordkette crest to the Zirbenweg, with the recovery days built in.

trips.title: Boardwalks and Bog, Running the Hautes Fagnes
trips.sub: Hautes Fagnes & Amblève Valley, Liège Province
trips.summary: A high-volume running week on Belgium's peat plateau, with two genuinely technical valley days in the Amblève gorges to break up the flat.

trips.title: Musala to Vihren: A Rila and Pirin Running Week Above 2,500 m
trips.summary: Two ranges, six days of running, and the two highest summits in the Balkans in the same week. Rila gives you granite slab, a hundred cirque lakes and dwarf-pine tunnels that will remove the skin from your shins.…

trips.title: Velebit Dry-Stone: Running the Premužić Trail
trips.summary: Velebit is a 145 km limestone wall standing between the Adriatic and the Lika plateau, and almost none of it holds water. That single fact shapes everything: the running is fast, pale, waterless and strangely engineered, because in 1930-33 the forestry engineer **Ante Premužić** cut a graded dry-stone path across the wildest section of the range, 57 km from Zavižan south to Baške Oštarije, laid so gently that a laden horse could walk it, threading between the Rožanski and Hajdučki kukovi towers without ever needing a hand. This week runs the northern half of that path properly, adds the botanical high ground around Zavižan, drops to Paklenica for the canyon and the Vaganski vrh ridge, and builds in one genuine rest day on the coast. It suits self-sufficient runners who are comfortable carrying two litres and reading a limestone landscape with no streams in it.

trips.title: The Main Ridge, Running the Krkonoše Border Path
trips.summary: Seven days on the Czech-Polish crest of the Krkonoše, from the Elbe source to Sněžka, using the boudy as water stops and the chairlifts as escape routes.

trips.title: Faroese Ridgelines: Streymoy & Vágar
trips.summary: A seven-day trail running itinerary in Streymoy, Vágar and Eysturoy, Faroe Islands.

trips.title: High Cols and Engraved Rock, Mercantour by Vésubie and Merveilles
trips.summary: A two-base week in the southern Alps, running the Vésubie cirques and the Vallée des Merveilles with no lifts and no shortcuts.

trips.title: The Balcons, A Chamonix Running Week Facing Mont Blanc
trips.summary: Seven days on the two great balcony trails of the Chamonix valley, with the lifts doing the climbing and the recovery days built into the plan.

trips.title: Watzmann Weeks, Running the Berchtesgaden Ridges
trips.summary: A coached week of ridge running in Berchtesgaden National Park, built around one big Watzmann day and supported by huts, boats and buses.

trips.title: Zagori & the Vikos Gorge
trips.summary: Zagori offers two entirely different running surfaces twenty minutes apart: the shaded limestone floor of the Vikos Gorge, 900 m deep from the Oxya rim to the Voidomatis bed, and the bare karst amphitheatre of Mt Tymfi above Papingo, where a 1,000 m climb lands you at a refuge on a 1,950 m col. Linking them are forty-six stone villages joined by 18th-century mule paths and single-arch packhorse bridges. The week's arc is deliberate: two orientation days, a two-day Tymfi block with a night at altitude, a genuine recovery day on the river, then a fast village-path day and a rim finish. It suits an experienced runner who wants technical volume without glacier travel.

trips.title: Blue Blazes and Dry Karst: A Trail-Running Week in the Bükk and the Mátra
trips.sub: Északi-középhegység, the Bükk and Mátra ranges
trips.summary: Hungary's mountains top out at 1,014 m, which is why runners underrate them and then get quietly taken apart. Seven days of beech singletrack, limestone rim path and the oldest waymarked long-distance trail in…

trips.title: Wicklow Granite: Dublin Mountains to Lugnaquilla
trips.summary: A seven-day trail running itinerary in County Wicklow / Dublin Mountains, Ireland.

trips.title: Cortina d'Ampezzo Ridgelines
trips.summary: Cortina sits at 1,224 m in a bowl ringed by Tofane, Cristallo, Sorapis, Croda da Lago and Nuvolau, and almost every classic run here is a lift-assisted or road-assisted ascent onto a limestone balcony followed by a very long, very technical descent. The week builds from the postcard laps, Tre Cime, Cinque Torri, Lago Federa, into two genuine ridge days on the Nuvolau-Averau crest and the Lagazuoi WWI tunnel system, with one full recovery day on the valley Dolomiti bike path. Trails are CAI-numbered, superbly signed and busy: the whole game is being on them at 07:00 rather than 11:00. It suits a confident mountain runner who can descend 1,200 m of scree and rock step without wrecking their quads on day two.

trips.title: The Principality Ridge, Fürstensteig and the Drei Schwestern
trips.summary: Liechtenstein's whole running country is one 25 km ridge, so you learn it, rehearse it, then run it end to end in a single day.

trips.title: Little Switzerland Underfoot, The Mullerthal Trail
trips.summary: Three linked Mullerthal Trail routes through sandstone crevices and beech plateau, run from Echternach on Luxembourg's free public transport.

trips.title: Sea Level to Summit, Running Monaco's Hinterland
trips.summary: A Riviera running week from a two-square-kilometre basecamp, climbing straight from the Mediterranean to the 900 m limestone ridges above Monaco.

trips.title: Durmitor Ridges
trips.sub: Durmitor National Park & Žabljak, northern Montenegro
trips.summary: Durmitor is a compact, savage limestone massif with 48 peaks over 2,000 m packed into an area you can drive across in forty minutes, and Žabljak at 1,456 m is the highest town in the Balkans, which means you sleep at altitude and start every run from a car park rather than a valley. The rock is pale, fluted karst with almost no soil, so the running is fast on the grass shelves and genuinely sharp on the ridges. The week arcs from a lake-circuit warm-up through the two showpiece summits, Bobotov Kuk and Prutaš, into a two-day Škrčka lakes excursion with a hut night, then a recovery day on the Tara canyon rim and a fast finish on Savin Kuk. It suits runners who like empty mountains, do not need refuge comfort, and can carry their own water.

trips.title: Romsdal Ridges: Åndalsnes Skyrunning Week
trips.summary: A seven-day trail running itinerary in Møre og Romsdal, Western Norway, Norway.

trips.title: Sandstone and Saucer: A Trail-Running Week in the Karkonosze and Góry Stołowe
trips.sub: The Sudetes, Karkonosze, Góry Stołowe and the Śnieżnik Massif
trips.summary: Two ranges, ninety kilometres apart, that run nothing alike. The Karkonosze give you a bald granite ridge on the Czech border, peat bog on duckboards, glacial cirques dropping away on your left, and stone-paved paths…

trips.title: Madeira: Pico Ruivo & the Levadas
trips.sub: Madeira, Central Massif, Laurissilva & the north coast
trips.summary: Madeira is a 1,862 m volcanic wall dropped into the Atlantic, and running it means alternating between two utterly different systems: the *veredas*, stone staircases cut along the ridges of the central massif with 500 m of air on both sides, and the *levadas*, 18th-century irrigation channels contouring for kilometres at a steady gradient through dripping laurel forest and pitch-dark tunnels. The week alternates hard massif days with flat levada days, which is both the smartest recovery structure available here and the way MIUT racers actually train. You will climb more stairs in seven days than in a year at home. It suits a runner with strong quads, no fear of exposure or of the dark, and the patience to deal with an official booking system for almost every trail.

trips.title: The Knife and the Plateau: Running Piatra Craiului and the Bucegi
trips.sub: Piatra Craiului & Bucegi Mountains, Southern Carpathians
trips.summary: Piatra Craiului is a 25 km limestone blade standing on end, and it is one of the few places in Europe where a runner meets fixed chains before breakfast. Then the Bucegi does the opposite: a vast tilted plateau at…

trips.title: Two Ridges, One Week: Running the Malá Fatra and the Low Tatras
trips.summary: The Krivánska Malá Fatra is Slovakia's most concentrated ridge, grass, limestone and chains packed into 20 km, and Veľký Rozsutec at the end of it is a rock horn you climb with your hands. Then you drive ninety…

trips.title: Julian Alps: Bohinj & Pokljuka
trips.sub: Gorenjska, Bohinj, Pokljuka & the Triglav Lakes Valley
trips.summary: Bohinj is the quiet end of the Julian Alps, a 525 m glacial lake with a 1,400 m wall of the Lower Bohinj range on one side and the Triglav massif on the other, and it gives a runner two contrasting playgrounds within twenty minutes. South and west: the Vogel-Rodica ridge and the Komna plateau, high, dry limestone with enormous views to Triglav. North and east: the Pokljuka plateau, a 1,200-1,400 m spruce-and-karst tableland whose *planine* (summer dairy pastures) link into some of the most runnable singletrack in the Alps. The week builds through a lake orientation day and a Vogel ridge day into an overnight in the Triglav Lakes Valley, then swings to Pokljuka for the Debela peč rim and the planina circuit, with a deliberate recovery day on the Bohinj lake path. It suits a runner who wants alpine scale, a functioning hut network and Slovenian prices.

trips.title: Sierra Nevada & Las Alpujarras
trips.sub: Andalucía, Sierra Nevada National Park & the Alpujarra Granadina
trips.summary: This week runs the biggest vertical relief in Western Europe outside the Alps: from white Berber-plan villages at 1,050 m to Mulhacén at 3,479 m, the highest ground on the Iberian mainland, in a single climb. The Alpujarra south slope gives you terraced chestnut and almond terrain threaded by *acequias*, Moorish snowmelt channels that double as the region's only reliable water, while the Granada north side gives the Vereda de la Estrella, a long, cool, glacial-valley approach to the north faces. The arc is deliberate: two acclimatisation days on the GR-7 and the acequia paths, a refuge night at 2,500 m, the Mulhacén day, a genuine recovery day in the gorge at Monachil, then a high traverse to finish. It suits a runner who is more worried about heat and altitude than about scrambling.

trips.title: Thin Air, The Engadin Ridge Week
trips.summary: Seven days of altitude running above Pontresina, from a 1,800 m valley floor to the 3,262 m summit of Piz Languard, with lifts and rail as the safety net.
